IUT4.ThmA.content: Diophantine inequality for hyperbolic curves: the height of omega_X(D) is bounded, up to a bounded discrepancy, by (1 + epsilon) times the sum of the log-different and the log-conductor on points of bounded degree.
explicit_hypotheses: X a smooth, proper, geometrically connected curve over a number field
D a reduced divisor, U_X = X minus D hyperbolic (deg omega_X(D) > 0)
d a positive integer, epsilon a positive real
implicit_hypotheses: heights, log-differents, log-conductors in the sense of [GenEll], Definitions 1.2 and 1.5
the relation <~ in the corrected sense of Remark 2.3.1 (ii)
IUT4.ThmA.conclusion: ht_{omega_X(D)} <~ (1 + epsilon)(log-diff_X + log-cond_D) on U_X(Qbar)^{<= d}.
obligations: Theorem A is Corollary 2.3; see that record.

The specialization to the abc inequality (X = P^1, D = {0, 1, infinity}, d = 1) is described in docs/PAPER_IV_DERIVATION.md. At the level of statements it is formalized in IUT4.ThmA.frag.equiv_abc: the special case for rational points is equivalent to Challenge.ABC. Not formalized: Theorem A itself, the identification of the height attached to omega_X(D) with Mathlib's logarithmic height, and the direction (ii) implies (i) of [GenEll] Theorem 2.1 that the passage from the proof in IUT IV to this special case uses. The bounded degree statement for P^1 minus {0, 1, infinity} implies Challenge.ABC through its degree one piece (IUT4.ThmA.frag.bounded_degree_implies_abc).

Page 3 asserts that the Vojta conjecture for hyperbolic curves, the ABC conjecture and the Szpiro conjecture for elliptic curves all follow as special cases of Theorem A, referring to [Vjt]; these derivations are not given in the paper.
ambiguities: Page 3 and page 54: the statements of Theorem A and Corollary 2.3 agree word for word (checked against both renders), except that Theorem A points to the notation of [GenEll] as recalled before Corollary 2.2.

IUT4.ThmA.frag.equiv_abc.content: VojtaLineMinusThreePointsRational is equivalent to Challenge.ABC; also the triple computations (height of a/c is log c, conductor is rad(abc)), the converse construction of a triple from x not in {0, 1}, invariance under bounded change of height, nonvacuity and the values at 1/2 and 8/9; invariance of ratConductor under x -> 1 - x and x -> 1/x, the bound log 2 on the change of height under x -> 1 - x, and the equivalence of VojtaLineMinusThreePointsRational with its restriction to 0 < x < 1 (same constant).
IUT4.ThmA.frag.equiv_abc.covers: Page 3: the sentence that the ABC Conjecture follows as a special case of Theorem A, for the rational-point specialization.
IUT4.ThmA.frag.equiv_abc.not_covered: Theorem A itself and its proof; the general equivalence with Vojta's conjecture for hyperbolic curves (IUT IV page 40, via GenEll Theorem 2.1, page 11), whose proof of (ii) implies (i) passes through points of degree d' = d deg(Y/X) > 1 and a noncritical Belyi map.

IUT4.ThmA.frag.bounded_degree_implies_ab.content: The degree one piece VojtaLineMinusThreePointsDegreeAtMost 1 is equivalent to VojtaLineMinusThreePointsRational, hence to Challenge.ABC; so VojtaLineMinusThreePointsBoundedDegree, and VojtaLineMinusThreePointsDegreeAtMost d for every d >= 1, imply Challenge.ABC (for d = 0 the statement is vacuous). The transport for fields of degree 1 uses the height of a rational number in any number field (heightNF_algebraMap_rat), invariance of the log-conductor and of the discriminant under ring isomorphisms, and the computation of the three functions at rational points (heightNF_rat, logDiffNF_rat, logCondNF_rat).
IUT4.ThmA.frag.bounded_degree_implies_ab.conclusion: VojtaLineMinusThreePointsDegreeAtMost 1 <-> Challenge.ABC; VojtaLineMinusThreePointsDegreeAtMost d -> Challenge.ABC for 1 <= d; VojtaLineMinusThreePointsBoundedDegree -> Challenge.ABC.
IUT4.ThmA.frag.bounded_degree_implies_ab.covers: Page 3, the sentence after Theorem A: 'the so-called Vojta Conjecture for hyperbolic curves, the ABC Conjecture, and the Szpiro Conjecture for elliptic curves all follow as special cases of Theorem A', for the ABC Conjecture through the bounded degree statement for P^1 minus {0, 1, infinity} at d = 1.
IUT4.ThmA.frag.bounded_degree_implies_ab.not_covered: Theorem A itself and its proof; the converse (Challenge.ABC does not by this file imply the statement for d > 1); the general equivalence with Vojta's conjecture for hyperbolic curves (IUT IV page 40, GenEll Theorem 2.1, page 11).

IUT4.Prop1_1.content: Multiple tensor products and differents. For a fixed index * in I and I* = I minus {*}, the normalization (R_I)^~ of the tensor product R_I = tensor over Z_p of the R_i satisfies p^{d_{I*}} (R_I)^~ inside R_I inside (R_I)^~, where d_{I*} is the sum of the orders d_i of the differents over i in I*.
explicit_hypotheses: p a prime number; I a finite set of cardinality >= 2
for i in I, k_i a finite extension of Q_p inside an algebraic closure of Q_p, R_i its ring of integers, d_i in Q_{>=0} the order of a generator of the different ideal of R_i over Z_p
for nonempty E in I: R_E = tensor product over Z_p of the R_i (i in E), d_E = sum of d_i (i in E)
a fixed element * of I, and I* = I minus {*}
implicit_hypotheses: ord is the p-adic valuation normalized by ord(p) = 1; p^lambda denotes an unspecified element of order lambda
(-)^~ is the normalization of the reduced ring in its ring of fractions
IUT4.Prop1_1.conclusion: p^{d_{I*}} (R_I)^~ is contained in R_I, which is contained in (R_I)^~; the left-hand side is well defined for suitable p^{d_{I*}}, for example products of elements p^{d_i} of R_i (i in I*).
definitions_required: R_I = tensor product of the R_i over Z_p
obligations: Not formalized: the inclusion p^(d_{I*}) (R_I)~ <= R_I, which needs the different of R_i over Z_p acting on the tensor product. For two factors, K_1 (x) K_2 is proved reduced and a finite product of finite extensions of Q_p (IUT4.Prop1_1.frag.vb_tensor_decomposition), the closed unit ball and integral closure models of R_i agree (IUT4.Prop1_1.frag.vb_integral_models), and R_E <= (R_E)~ is proved with (R_E)~ the integral closure of Z_p in K_1 (x) K_2 (IUT4.Prop1_1.frag.packet_integers). More than two factors, and that this integral closure is the normalization of R_E in its ring of fractions, are open.

IUT4.Prop1_1.frag.vb_tensor_decompositio.content: For finite extensions K1, K2 of Q_p: K1 (x)_{Q_p} K2 is formally unramified over Q_p, reduced, and isomorphic as a Q_p-algebra to a finite product of finite separable field extensions of Q_p.
explicit_hypotheses: K1, K2 fields with finite-dimensional Q_p-algebra structures
IUT4.Prop1_1.frag.vb_tensor_decompositio.conclusion: IsReduced (K1 (x) K2); an algebra isomorphism K1 (x) K2 = product of finitely many fields A_i, each finite-dimensional and separable over Q_p.
IUT4.Prop1_1.frag.vb_tensor_decompositio.covers: Page 9: the ambient ring K1 (x) K2 of R_E (the paper's tensor product over Z_p, tensored up to Q_p) is reduced; page 13: tensor products of finite extensions decompose as direct sums of finitely many finite extensions of Q_p. Two factors.
IUT4.Prop1_1.frag.vb_tensor_decompositio.not_covered: More than two factors; that the ring of fractions of R_E is K1 (x) K2; the inclusion p^(d_{I*}) (R_I)^~ subset R_I.
ambiguities: Pages 9 and 13 take tensor products over Z_p; the Q_p form K1 (x)_{Q_p} K2 is used, and the identification with K1 (x)_{Z_p} K2 is not formalized.
IUT4.Prop1_1.frag.vb_tensor_decompositio.scope: two factors K1, K2 (finite extensions of Q_p); (R_E)^~ = padicPacketNormalization (elements of K1 (x) K2 integral over Z_p); mu^log = padicPacketMuLog in Module.finBasis coordinates

IUT4.Prop1_1.frag.vb_integral_models.content: For a finite extension A of Q_p, x is integral over Z_p (padicVolIntegral) iff its spectral norm is at most 1; in a finite product of Q_p-algebras an element is integral over Z_p iff each component is.
explicit_hypotheses: A a field with a finite-dimensional Q_p-algebra structure (first statement)
a finite family of commutative Q_p-algebras (second statement)
IUT4.Prop1_1.frag.vb_integral_models.conclusion: padicVolIntegral p x <-> spectralNorm x <= 1; padicVolIntegral p x <-> for all i, padicVolIntegral p (x i).
IUT4.Prop1_1.frag.vb_integral_models.covers: Page 9: R_i the ring of integers of k_i, and the normalization (-)^~ of R_E; identifies the closed unit ball model and the integral closure model of R_i used by the packet definitions.
IUT4.Prop1_1.frag.vb_integral_models.not_covered: The normalization of R_E in its ring of fractions as such; Proposition 1.1's inclusion.
IUT4.Prop1_1.frag.vb_integral_models.scope: two factors K1, K2 (finite extensions of Q_p); (R_E)^~ = padicPacketNormalization (elements of K1 (x) K2 integral over Z_p); mu^log = padicPacketMuLog in Module.finBasis coordinates

IUT4.Prop1_1.frag.packet_integers.content: For two finite extensions K_1, K_2 of Q_p: R_E is defined as the additive span in K_1 tensor K_2 of x tensor y with x, y integral over Z_p, and (R_E)~ as the elements of K_1 tensor K_2 integral over Z_p; R_E is contained in (R_E)~.
explicit_hypotheses: K_1, K_2 fields that are Q_p-algebras
IUT4.Prop1_1.frag.packet_integers.conclusion: padicPacketIntegers p K_1 K_2 is a subset of padicPacketNormalization p K_1 K_2.
IUT4.Prop1_1.frag.packet_integers.covers: Page 9, Proposition 1.1: the definitions of R_E and of its normalization (R_E)~ and the inclusion R_I <= (R_I)~ of its proof, for two factors; page 14 uses this inclusion as mu^log(R_I) <= mu^log((R_I)~).
IUT4.Prop1_1.frag.packet_integers.not_covered: The identification of the integral closure of Z_p in K_1 tensor K_2 with the normalization of R_E in its ring of fractions; compactness and openness of (R_E)~ (proved for two factors in IUT4.Prop1_4.frag.vb_packet_normalization); p^(d_I*) . (R_I)~ <= R_I; more than two factors.
ambiguities: (R_E)~ is taken as the integral closure of Z_p in K_1 tensor K_2; equality with the normalization of R_E in its ring of fractions is not formalized.

IUT4.Prop1_2.content: Defines a_i = (1/e_i) ceil(e_i/(p-2)) (p > 2), a_i = 2 (p = 2), b_i = floor(log(p e_i/(p-1))/log p) − 1/e_i, and bounds p-adic logarithms of unit groups and automorphisms of their tensor products by powers of p.
explicit_hypotheses: the notation of Proposition 1.1 (p, I, k_i, R_i, d_i)
e_i the ramification index of k_i over Q_p
phi an automorphism of the Q_p-vector space log_p(R_I^x) tensor Q_p that induces an automorphism of the submodule log_p(R_I^x)
lambda in (1/e_i) Z, i in I (in (ii), (iii))
(iii): p > 2 and e_i <= p - 2 for all i; (iv): p > 2 and e_i = 1 for all i
IUT4.Prop1_2.conclusion: (i) p^{a_i} R_i in log_p(R_i^x) in p^{-b_i} R_i, with equalities if p > 2 and e_i <= p-2; (ii) phi(p^lambda (R_I)^~) in p^{floor(lambda - d_I - a_I)} log_p(R_I^x) in p^{floor(lambda - d_I - a_I) - b_I} (R_I)^~; (iii) phi(p^lambda (R_I)^~) in p^{lambda - d_I - 1} (R_I)^~; (iv) phi((R_I)^~) in (R_I)^~.
obligations: The inclusions (ii) to (iv) need the tensor products R_I and Proposition 1.1; not formalized. Assertion (i) is proved for k_i = Q_p (IUT4.Prop1_2.frag.log_series_def, IUT4.Prop1_2.frag.log_series_norm, IUT4.Prop1_2.frag.log_hom, IUT4.Prop1_2.frag.i_Qp), for finite extensions of Q_p in a normed-field model with a hypothesis on e (IUT4.Prop1_2.frag.i_model, IUT4.Prop1_2.frag.i_equality_model), and for every finite extension L of Q_p with R_i = integralClosure Z_p L, e_i = Ideal.ramificationIdx and the spectral norm, with no hypothesis on the norm (IUT4.Prop1_2.frag.bridge_i). No declaration states the whole proposition.
Elementary facts about a_i, b_i used in the proof are checked in the fragments listed in `fragments`.
ambiguities: The text extraction drops the ceiling in a_i and the floor in b_i; the render of page 10 shows both.

IUT4.Prop1_2.frag.a_b_of_le.content: For natural numbers p, e with 2 < p and 1 <= e <= p - 2, the real numbers a(p, e) = (1/e) ceil(e/(p-2)) and b(p, e) = floor(log(p e/(p-1))/log p) - 1/e satisfy a = 1/e and b = -1/e.
IUT4.Prop1_2.frag.a_b_of_le.conclusion: a p e = 1/e and b p e = -(1/e).
IUT4.Prop1_2.frag.a_b_of_le.covers: Page 10, the sentence 'if p > 2 and e_i <= p - 2, then a_i = 1/e_i = -b_i'.
IUT4.Prop1_2.frag.a_b_of_le.not_covered: Everything about rings, logarithms and inclusions.

IUT4.Prop1_2.frag.a_b_of_e_one.not_covered: d_I = 0, the integrality a_I in Z, and the inclusion of (iv).

IUT4.Prop1_2.frag.log_series_def.content: Definition of the p-adic logarithm on the open unit disc of Q_p: log(1 + x) = sum over n >= 1 of (-1)^(n+1) x^n / n (as a tsum; a junk value where the series does not converge), together with the logarithm of a unit u of Z_p defined as (p - 1)^(-1) log(u^(p-1)).
IUT4.Prop1_2.frag.log_series_def.conclusion: padicLogOnePlus p x and padicLogUnit p u are defined.
IUT4.Prop1_2.frag.log_series_def.covers: Page 10: the notation log_p(-) for the p-adic logarithm, for the base field Q_p.
IUT4.Prop1_2.frag.log_series_def.not_covered: Finite extensions k_i of Q_p and tensor products; all of the inclusions (i) to (iv).
ambiguities: The pages read do not fix the extension of log_p from 1 + p Z_p to Z_p^x; (p - 1)^(-1) log(u^(p-1)) is used.
IUT4.Prop1_2.frag.log_series_def.scope: base field Q_p only; finite extensions of Q_p are not treated

IUT4.Prop1_2.frag.log_series_norm.content: For a prime p and x in Q_p with |x| <= 1/p* (p* = p for odd p, 4 for p = 2): |log(1 + x)| = |x|. Supporting lemmas: the series converges for |x| < 1, log(1 + 0) = 0, and padicLogOnePlus p x = NormedSpace.log (1 + x) for all x.
IUT4.Prop1_2.frag.log_series_norm.covers: Page 11, proof of (i): the appeal to the well-known theory of the p-adic logarithm ([Kobl], p. 81), in the case k_i = Q_p.
IUT4.Prop1_2.frag.log_series_norm.not_covered: Finite extensions of Q_p; the inclusions themselves (see the fragment i_Qp).
IUT4.Prop1_2.frag.log_series_norm.scope: base field Q_p only; finite extensions of Q_p are not treated

IUT4.Prop1_2.frag.log_hom.content: Homomorphism property of the p-adic logarithm series on the open unit disc of Q_p: for |x| < 1 and |y| < 1, log(1 + (x + y + xy)) = log(1 + x) + log(1 + y). The derived lemma padicLogUnit_mul states that log on Z_p^x is a homomorphism.
explicit_hypotheses: x, y in Q_p with |x| < 1 and |y| < 1
IUT4.Prop1_2.frag.log_hom.conclusion: padicLogOnePlus p (x + y + x * y) = padicLogOnePlus p x + padicLogOnePlus p y.
IUT4.Prop1_2.frag.log_hom.covers: Page 10: the display defining log_p(R_E^x) as the tensor product over Z_p of the log_p(R_i^x), which treats log_p(R_i^x) as a Z_p-module, for k_i = Q_p.
IUT4.Prop1_2.frag.log_hom.not_covered: Finite extensions of Q_p; the inclusions of (i) to (iv).
IUT4.Prop1_2.frag.log_hom.scope: base field Q_p only; finite extensions of Q_p are not treated

IUT4.Prop1_2.frag.i_Qp.content: Proposition 1.2 (i) for k_i = Q_p (e_i = 1, R_i = Z_p), with log on Z_p^x taken as (p - 1)^(-1) log(u^(p-1)): log(Z_p^x) is the closed ball of radius 1/p* in Q_p (p* = p for odd p, 4 for p = 2). Corollaries in the lemmas: for p != 2 it is the closed ball of radius 1/p, that is p Z_p (a = 1, b = -1, with equalities as the paper asserts for p > 2 and e_i <= p - 2); for p = 2, the closed ball of radius 1/4 is contained in it and it is contained in the closed unit ball, that is 4 Z_2 in log(Z_2^x) in Z_2 (a = 2, b = 0).
IUT4.Prop1_2.frag.i_Qp.conclusion: range (u in Z_p^x mapsto padicLogUnit p u) = {z in Q_p : |z| <= 1/p*}.
IUT4.Prop1_2.frag.i_Qp.covers: Page 10, display (i): p^(a_i) R_i in log_p(R_i^x) in p^(-b_i) R_i, with equalities for p > 2 and e_i <= p - 2, in the case k_i = Q_p (e_i = 1).
IUT4.Prop1_2.frag.i_Qp.not_covered: Ramified or nontrivial finite extensions k_i; assertions (ii) to (iv). For p = 2 the Lean result is sharper than the paper's inclusions (it proves log(Z_2^x) = 4 Z_2).
ambiguities: The pages read do not fix the extension of log_p from 1 + p Z_p to Z_p^x; (p - 1)^(-1) log(u^(p-1)) is used and recorded in the module docstring.
IUT4.Prop1_2.frag.i_Qp.scope: base field Q_p only; finite extensions of Q_p are not treated

IUT4.Prop1_2.frag.bridge_ring_of_integer.content: For x in a finite extension L of Q_p with its spectral norm: |x| <= 1 iff x is integral over Z_p; hence the closed unit ball equals integralClosure Z_p L as a set, and |x| = 1 iff x is a unit of integralClosure Z_p L, so the unit sphere is the image of its unit group.
explicit_hypotheses: L a field with a finite-dimensional Q_p-algebra structure and a compatible Z_p-algebra structure (IsScalarTower Z_p Q_p L)
L normed by the spectral norm
IUT4.Prop1_2.frag.bridge_ring_of_integer.conclusion: spectral norm of x is at most 1 iff IsIntegral Z_p x; the closed unit ball is integralClosure Z_p L; the unit sphere is the image of (integralClosure Z_p L)^x.
IUT4.Prop1_2.frag.bridge_ring_of_integer.covers: Page 9: R_i is the ring of integers of k_i; page 10: R_i^x in Proposition 1.2 (i). Identifies the closed-ball model of the normed-field fragments with the ring of integers.
IUT4.Prop1_2.frag.bridge_ring_of_integer.not_covered: The uniqueness of the norm on k_i (the spectral norm is fixed); tensor products R_I.
IUT4.Prop1_2.frag.bridge_ring_of_integer.scope: finite extension L of Q_p (Field, finite-dimensional Q_p-algebra, compatible Z_p-algebra) with Mathlib's spectral norm spectralNorm Q_p L; R_i = integralClosure Z_p L; e_i = Ideal.ramificationIdx of a prime P over pZ_p (proved unique)

IUT4.Prop1_2.frag.bridge_ramification.content: The ring of integers R of L is local with maximal ideal {|x| < 1}, a discrete valuation ring; its maximal ideal lies over pZ_p and is the only prime over pZ_p. For such a prime P with e = P.ramificationIdx Z_p there is an irreducible w of R with P = (w), (p) = (w)^e as ideals, 0 < |w| < 1, |w|^e = 1/p, |x| = |w|^k (k an integer) for every nonzero x of L, and |x| <= |w| when |x| < 1. The image of the norm on L^x is {p^(k/e) : k integer}; |x|^e <= 1/p for |x| < 1, and e is the least natural number with this property.
explicit_hypotheses: L a field with a finite-dimensional Q_p-algebra structure and a compatible Z_p-algebra structure (IsScalarTower Z_p Q_p L)
L normed by the spectral norm
P a prime ideal of integralClosure Z_p L lying over the maximal ideal pZ_p
IUT4.Prop1_2.frag.bridge_ramification.conclusion: e = P.ramificationIdx Z_p satisfies the hypothesis hval of the normed-field model and no smaller natural number does; the value group is p^((1/e)Z).
IUT4.Prop1_2.frag.bridge_ramification.covers: Page 10: e_i, the ramification index of k_i over Q_p, and the normalization ord(p) = 1 of page 9 (ord(L^x) = (1/e_i)Z).

IUT4.Prop1_2.frag.bridge_ramification.scope: finite extension L of Q_p (Field, finite-dimensional Q_p-algebra, compatible Z_p-algebra) with Mathlib's spectral norm spectralNorm Q_p L; R_i = integralClosure Z_p L; e_i = Ideal.ramificationIdx of a prime P over pZ_p (proved unique)

P a prime ideal of integralClosure Z_p L lying over the maximal ideal pZ_p

IUT4.Prop1_2.frag.bridge_fractional_idea.scope: finite extension L of Q_p (Field, finite-dimensional Q_p-algebra, compatible Z_p-algebra) with Mathlib's spectral norm spectralNorm Q_p L; R_i = integralClosure Z_p L; e_i = Ideal.ramificationIdx of a prime P over pZ_p (proved unique)

IUT4.Prop1_2.frag.ext_log_hom.content: For a prime p and a complete normed field K that is a normed Q_p-algebra: the series converges for |x| < 1, equals NormedSpace.log (1 + x), and satisfies log(1 + (x + y + xy)) = log(1 + x) + log(1 + y) for |x|, |y| < 1; hence log((1 + x)^n - 1) = n log(1 + x). The logarithm of units satisfies extLogUnit u = N^(-1) log(u^N) for every N > 0 with |u^N - 1| < 1, extLogUnit(1 + x) = log(1 + x) for |x| < 1, extLogUnit(u^m) = m extLogUnit u and extLogUnit(uv) = extLogUnit u + extLogUnit v when u^N, v^N lie in the open disc around 1; in a locally compact K every u with |u| = 1 has such an N, and the least one is prime to p when |u| <= 1.
explicit_hypotheses: K a normed field and normed Q_p-algebra, complete
IUT4.Prop1_2.frag.ext_log_hom.conclusion: extLogOnePlus (x + y + x*y) = extLogOnePlus x + extLogOnePlus y.

IUT4.Prop1_2.frag.ext_log_isometry.content: For a prime p and a complete normed field K that is a normed Q_p-algebra: |log(1 + x)| = |x| when p |x|^(p-1) < 1, a condition equivalent to |x| < p^(-1/(p-1)); |log(1 + a) - log(1 + b)| = |a - b| on that disc, so x -> log(1 + x) is injective there; at the boundary p |x|^(p-1) = 1 the p-th term has norm |x|; for 0 <= r with p r^(p-1) < 1, x -> log(1 + x) maps the closed ball of radius r onto itself (surjectivity by the contraction mapping principle).

IUT4.Prop1_3.content: Estimates of differents: d_i >= d_0 + (e_{i/0} − 1)/e_i, with equality if tame; and d_i <= d_0 + n_i + 1/e_0 when k_i is Galois over a tame extension of k_0.

(ii): k_i finite Galois over a subfield k_1 with k_0 in k_1 and k_1 tamely ramified over k_0
IUT4.Prop1_3.conclusion: (i) d_i >= d_0 + (e_{i/0} - 1)/(e_{i/0} e_0) = d_0 + (e_{i/0} - 1)/e_i, with equality if k_i is tamely ramified over k_0; (ii) d_i <= d_0 + n_i + 1/e_0.
obligations: Proposition 1.3 over a general base k_0 (the transitivity of the different over R_0, ramification in towers) and (ii) beyond its base case (Galois and Kummer extensions, the bound n_i) are not formalized. For k_0 = Q_p: the lower bound of (i) is proved for rings of integers of finite extensions of Q_p (IUT4.Prop1_3.frag.i_differentOrder_ge, IUT4.Prop1_3.frag.i_differentOrder_ge_tower, IUT4.Prop1_3.frag.i_padic_differentOrder_ge), the prime over p is unique (IUT.PaperIV.LocalFields.padicBridge_prime_eq_maximalIdeal), the equality in the tame case, the strict inequality in the wild case and their equivalence are proved (IUT4.Prop1_3.frag.i_tame_equality_padic, IUT4.Prop1_3.frag.i_wild_inequality_padic, IUT4.Prop1_3.frag.i_equality_iff_tame_padic), and (ii) is proved in its base case k_1 = k_i tame over Q_p (IUT4.Prop1_3.frag.ii_base_padic). IUT4.Prop1_3.frag.i_tame_equality_padic.content: For a finite extension L of Q_p and a prime P of its ring of integers over p with ramification index e: if p does not divide e, the exponent of P in the different (differentExponent Z_p R P) equals e - 1; equivalently differentOrder Z_p R P = (e - 1)/e. Proof: pR = P^e; the trace of R/P^n over F_p is n times the trace of R/P (additivity of the trace along 0 -> R/P -> R/P^(n+1) -> R/P^n -> 0); R/P is separable over the finite field F_p, so some trace is nonzero, and since p does not divide e some element of R has a unit trace in Z_p, which forbids P^e from dividing the different.
explicit_hypotheses: L a field with a finite-dimensional Q_p-algebra structure and a compatible Z_p-algebra structure (IsScalarTower Z_p Q_p L)
P a prime ideal of R = integralClosure Z_p L lying over the maximal ideal pZ_p
p does not divide P.ramificationIdx Z_p

Proof: every trace from R to Z_p is divisible by p (it is e times a residue trace modulo p), so P^e divides the different.

IUT4.Prop1_4.content: Normalized log-volume estimates for p-adic tensor packets: normalization of mu^log, the value of mu^log(log_p(R_i^x)), and upper bounds for the log-volumes of the regions containing phi(p^lambda (R_I)^~).
explicit_hypotheses: the notation of Proposition 1.2; R_i^mu the torsion of R_i^x, p^{f_i} the residue field cardinality, p^{m_i} the order of the p-primary part of R_i^mu
(iii): I* a subset of I with p - 2 >= e_i for all i in I minus I*; lambda in (1/e_{i_dagger}) Z, i_dagger in I
(iv): p > 2 and e_i = 1 for all i in I
IUT4.Prop1_4.conclusion: (i) a normalized log-volume mu^log on compact open subsets of finite extensions of Q_p and of their tensor products, with mu^log(R_i) = 0, mu^log(p R_i) = -log p, mu^log((R_E)^~) = 0, mu^log(p (R_E)^~) = -log p; (ii) mu^log(log_p(R_i^x)) = -(1/e_i + m_i/(e_i f_i)) log p; (iii) the inclusions phi(p^lambda (R_I)^~) in p^{floor(lambda - d_I - a_I)} log_p(R_I^x) in p^{floor(lambda - d_I - a_I) - b_I} (R_I)^~, the bounds mu^log(p^{floor(lambda-d_I-a_I)} log_p(R_I^x)) <= (-lambda + d_I + 1 + 4|I*|/p) log p and mu^log(p^{floor(lambda-d_I-a_I)-b_I} (R_I)^~) <= (-lambda + d_I + 1) log p + sum_{i in I*} {3 + log e_i}, and d_I + a_I >= |I| (p > 2), >= 2|I| (p = 2); (iv) phi((R_I)^~) in (R_I)^~ and mu^log((R_I)^~) = 0.
obligations: The log-volume of [AbsTopIII], Proposition 5.7, is not read; mu^log is modeled as log(mu(A)/mu(R))/d for a Haar measure mu (IUT4.Prop1_4.frag.muLog_def), an interpretation. With it the normalization (i) is proved for one finite extension of Q_p on its ring of integers (IUT4.Prop1_4.frag.vb_field_normalization) and for tensor packets of two factors on (R_E)~ (IUT4.Prop1_4.frag.vb_packet_normalization); more than two factors are open. The value (ii) is obtained only for p > 2 and e_i <= p - 2 and only when m_i = 0, which is not proved (IUT4.Prop1_4.frag.vb_logunit_eq_of_le); otherwise only bounds are proved (IUT4.Prop1_4.frag.logUnit_bounds, IUT4.Prop1_4.frag.vb_logunit_bounds). The inclusions of (iii) and (iv), which need Proposition 1.1, and the additivity over tensor factors used on page 14 are not formalized.

The arithmetic fragments check the proof starting from supplied volume bounds; the per-index inequality d_i + a_i >= 1 (2 for p = 2) is proved for actual finite extensions of Q_p (IUT4.Prop1_4.frag.bridge_d_add_a). None of the fragments establishes the containments of (iii) and (iv).
ambiguities: The first display of (iii) writes p^{lambda − d_I − a_I}; the render shows a floor, which accounts for the +1.

IUT4.Prop1_4.frag.measure_smul.content: For every additive Haar measure mu on a d-dimensional normed Q_p-vector space V, every nonzero c in Q_p and every set A: mu(c A) = |c|_p^d mu(A).

mu an additive Haar measure on V

explicit_hypotheses: V a finite-dimensional normed Q_p-vector space of dimension d with its Borel sigma-algebra
mu an additive Haar measure on V
IUT4.Prop1_4.frag.muLog_def.conclusion: padicMuLog p mu Lambda A and padicMuLogE p mu Lambda A are defined.

ambiguities: The normalization by the two values mu^log(R_i) = 0 and mu^log(p . R_i) = -log(p) determines log(mu(-)/mu(R_i))/d among functions of the form alpha log mu + beta; that the paper's mu^log has this form is an interpretation.

IUT4.Prop1_4.frag.muLog_laws.content: Laws of the normalized log-volume: mu^log(p^n . A) = mu^log(A) - n log p for n an integer, when A and Lambda have positive finite measure and d > 0; also mu^log(Lambda) = 0, mu^log(c A) = mu^log(A) + log|c|, translation invariance, monotonicity on sets of positive finite measure, independence of the Haar measure and of a continuous linear change of coordinates; the EReal form is monotone and equals the real form on sets of positive finite measure.
explicit_hypotheses: V a finite-dimensional normed Q_p-vector space of dimension d with its Borel sigma-algebra
mu an additive Haar measure on V
IUT4.Prop1_4.frag.muLog_laws.conclusion: padicMuLog p mu Lambda (p^n . A) = padicMuLog p mu Lambda A - n log p.
IUT4.Prop1_4.frag.muLog_laws.covers: Page 13, Proposition 1.4 (i): mu^log(p . R_i) = -log(p) and the scaling law used in the proof of (iii) on page 14 (mu^log(p^k . M) = mu^log(M) - k log p).

R modeled as the closed unit ball of K

IUT4.Prop1_5.content: Archimedean metric estimates: C tensor_R C = C + C is compatible with metrics up to a factor 2; primitive automorphisms preserve decompositions; M_I splits into 2^{|I|-1}|V|^{|I|} copies of C with metric factor 2^{|I|-1}; tensor products of vectors of length lambda lie in lambda^{|I|} B_I.

(iii), (iv): I, V nonempty finite sets; M = direct sum of copies C_v (v in V); M_I = tensor product over R of copies M_i of M; B_I the product of unit balls
(iv): lambda > 0 and m_i in M_i whose components have length lambda
implicit_hypotheses: (i): the isomorphism C tensor_R C -> C + C is any isomorphism of topological rings (one arising from the Chinese remainder theorem); the primitive automorphisms form a group of order 8
IUT4.Prop1_5.conclusion: (i) C tensor_R C = C + C is compatible with the metrics up to a factor 2; (ii) the decomposition is preserved by primitive automorphisms; (iii) M_I is a direct sum of 2^{|I|-1}|V|^{|I|} copies of C, with direct sum metric 2^{|I|-1} times the tensor metric, and B_I is preserved; (iv) the tensor product of the m_i lies in lambda^{|I|} B_I.

ambiguities: Page 15, (i): 'compatible up to a factor of 2' refers to the metric (the square of the length); the bracket says lengths differ by a factor sqrt(2). The fragment crt_normSq checks the squared-norm form.

IUT4.Prop1_5.frag.crt_pure.not_covered: That crt is a ring isomorphism of the tensor product (only pure tensors are checked), and the tensor product itself.

IUT4.Prop1_6.content: Consequence of the prime number theorem: n <= 4 p_n / (3 log p_n) for n large, and pi(eta) <= 4 eta/(3 log eta) for eta >= eta_prm.

IUT4.Rem1_7_1.content: When Proposition 1.7 is used in Theorem 1.10 for packet-normalized log-volumes, the computation uses the normalized log-volumes of Proposition 1.4 (i) instead of the non-normalized log-volumes for which the weights of IUT III Remark 3.1.1 (ii) were computed. Hence the weights [K_v : (F_mod)_v]^{-1} must be replaced by [K_v : Q_{v_Q}] [K_v : (F_mod)_v]^{-1} = [(F_mod)_v : Q_{v_Q}], and the normalized weights by prod_{alpha in A} [(F_mod)_{v_alpha} : Q_{v_Q}] divided by the sum over all collections {w_alpha}_{alpha in A} (not necessarily distinct) of elements of V_mod over v_Q of prod_{alpha in A} [(F_mod)_{w_alpha} : Q_{v_Q}]. These are the weights lambda_{Pi e dagger} / sum_{e in E^n} lambda_{Pi e} of Proposition 1.7 with E the places of V (equivalently V_mod) over a fixed v_Q, n = |A| with A = {alpha_1, ..., alpha_n}, lambda_e = [(F_mod)_v : Q_{v_Q}] > 0 for e corresponding to v, and beta_e a normalized log-volume of a compact open subset of K_v.

implicit_hypotheses: the bijection V -> V_mod (underline v to v) restricted to places over a fixed v_Q

obligations: A change of normalization stated without proof; the identity [K_v : Q_{v_Q}] [K_v : (F_mod)_v]^{-1} = [(F_mod)_v : Q_{v_Q}] is the tower law for degrees.

IUT4.Prop1_8.content: Torsion points of elliptic curves over a perfect field k: Serre's criterion; the exact sequence of automorphism groups, the minimal field of definition and models; the 2-torsion representation; uniqueness of models with rational l-torsion; semistable reduction from rational l-torsion; the Legendre form; ramification of torsion fields.
explicit_hypotheses: k a perfect field, kbar an algebraic closure, G_k = Gal(kbar/k)
(i): l >= 3 a prime invertible in k, k = kbar, A an abelian variety over k with a polarization lambda
(ii): E_kbar an elliptic curve over kbar with origin; n a positive integer
(iv): as (ii), l >= 3 a prime invertible in k, E'_k and E''_k models over k with all l-torsion rational over k
(v): as (ii), k a complete discrete valuation field with ring of integers O_k, l >= 3 a prime invertible in O_k, E_k a model over k with all l-torsion rational
(vi): as (iii), 2 invertible in k, G_E = G_k, and G_E -> Aut(E_kbar[2]) trivial; for the second part k a complete discrete valuation field with 2 invertible in O_k
(vii): as (ii), k a complete discrete valuation field, E_k a model over k, n invertible in O_k
IUT4.Prop1_8.conclusion: (i) Aut_k(A, lambda) -> Aut(A[l]) is injective; (ii) an exact sequence 1 -> Aut_kbar(E_kbar) -> Aut_k(E_kbar) -> G_k with open image G_E, a representation rho_n on E_kbar[n], k_E = field of definition = k(j), and models over k_H correspond to sections over H; (iii) rho_2 factors through G_E -> Aut(E_kbar[2]); (iv) E'_k is isomorphic to E''_k; (v) E_k has semistable reduction over O_k; (vi) E_kbar descends to E_k over k in Legendre form, which has semistable reduction over O_k' for some k'/k with [k' : k] <= 2, and k' = k is possible if E_k has good reduction over O_k'; (vii) good reduction gives G_k acting unramified on E_kbar[n], and bad multiplicative reduction gives a tamely ramified extension with ramification index dividing n.

IUT4.Thm1_10.StepIV.content: To estimate C_Theta one must bound from above the procession-normalized mono-analytic log-volume of the holomorphic hull of the union of possible images of a Theta-pilot object, relative to the Kummer isomorphisms, in the multiradial representation of IUT III Theorem 3.11 (i), subject to the indeterminacies (Ind1), (Ind2), (Ind3). This is done at each v_Q in V_Q: for each j in {1, ..., l*} one bounds the component in I^Q(S^pm_{j+1}; n,o D^|-_{v_Q}) and then averages over j. Since S^pm_{j+1} = {0, 1, ..., j} and that object is a tensor product of j+1 copies of the direct sum of the Q-spans of the log-shells at the elements of V(F_mod)_{v_Q}, one bounds, for each collection {v_i}_{i in S^pm_{j+1}} of (not necessarily distinct) elements of V(F_mod)_{v_Q}, the component for the tensor product of the Q-spans of the corresponding log-shells, and then takes the weighted average over all such collections as in Remark 1.7.1.

IUT4.Rem1_10_1.content: A motivation of the series was to build a framework in which an analogue of the scheme-theoretic Hodge-Arakelov theory of [HASurI], [HASurII] avoids the obstructions to diophantine applications met there. The computation of the leading term ((l*+3)/2) log(d_{v_Q}^K) - ((2l*+1)(l*+1)/(12l)) log(q_{v_Q}) in the final display of Step (v) of the proof of Theorem 1.10, via (E1), (E2), is described as essentially identical to the computation of the leading term in the proof of [HASurI], Theorem A; the author states the computations were essentially known around 2000 and the problem was to construct a framework in which to perform them, comparing this with the Weil conjectures before Weil cohomology and with computations motivated by physics.
explicit_hypotheses: the notation of Theorem 1.10 and of Step (v) of its proof
IUT4.Rem1_10_1.conclusion: An informal comparison: the leading term ((l*+3)/2) log(d_{v_Q}^K) - ((2l*+1)(l*+1)/(12l)) log(q_{v_Q}) of Step (v) arises from (E1), (E2) as in the proof of [HASurI], Theorem A. No mathematical assertion is made that needs proof.
obligations: Nothing to prove; a heuristic and historical remark.
ambiguities: Page 31: 'essentially identical' is not made precise; the corresponding computation of [HASurI] is not reproduced.

IUT4.Rem1_10_2.content: The computation of Theorem 1.10 is viewed as a derivative in the F_l^* direction, corresponding under the analogy with p-adic Teichmueller theory ([pOrd], [pTeich]) to the derivative of the canonical Frobenius lifting. In [HASurII], Corollary 3.6, a portion of the arithmetic Kodaira-Spencer morphism coincides with the geometric one; in terms of the action of GL_2(F_l) on l-torsion this portion is given by the unipotent matrices, whereas the F_l^*-symmetries of the present papers correspond to the toral (diagonal) matrices. For large l, GL_2(F_l) is a good approximation of GL_2(Z) or GL_2(R), where toral subgroups correspond to isotropy subgroups (isomorphic to S^1) of points of the upper half-plane, a group-theoretic representation of tangent vectors.
IUT4.Rem1_10_2.conclusion: An analogy: the computation of Theorem 1.10 is a derivative in the F_l^*-direction; F_l^*-symmetries correspond to toral matrices of GL_2(F_l), in contrast with the unipotent matrices relevant to the arithmetic Kodaira-Spencer morphism of [HASurII]. No assertion needing proof.
obligations: Nothing to prove; a heuristic remark.

IUT4.Rem1_10_3.content: The terms involving l in the final display of Theorem 1.10 are presented as an inevitable consequence of the role of l-torsion points. It is said to be crucial to work over the field of rationality K of the l-torsion points (not over F) both for the global portions of the Theta NF- and Theta^{pm ell}-Hodge theaters and for their local portions (prime-strips), which are needed to glue these into a Theta^{pm ell} NF-Hodge theater; allowing any Galois indeterminacy on l-torsion points, even at v in V^good intersect V^non, would invalidate the manipulations of IUT I, sections 4 and 6.
explicit_hypotheses: the notation of Theorem 1.10; K = F(E_F[l])
IUT4.Rem1_10_3.conclusion: An explanatory claim: working over K, including at the prime-strips at good nonarchimedean places, is necessary for the gluing of IUT I (Propositions 4.7, 6.5), and this produces the terms in l of Theorem 1.10. Stated without proof.
obligations: The claim that Galois indeterminacy at the l-torsion points would invalidate IUT I, sections 4 and 6, is asserted, not derived here.

IUT4.Rem1_10_4.content: The fluctuations of log-volume from the multiradial representation of IUT III Theorem 3.11 (i), computed in Theorem 1.10, are called inter-universal analytic torsion, analytic torsion being read as a metrized measure of the deviation of holomorphic functions from real analytic ones. Three cases: (a) in classical Arakelov theory, analytic torsion is the logarithm of a normalized determinant of a Laplacian, depending on the Kaehler metric and hence on the holomorphic moduli ([Arak]); (b) in scheme-theoretic Hodge-Arakelov theory, the comparison isomorphism of [HASurI] Theorem A and its Gaussian poles measure a discrepancy of integral structures near infinity, an analytic torsion at the divisor at infinity; (c) in IUT, the fluctuations come from comparing an alien arithmetic holomorphic structure with the multiradial representation, the object compared being values of the theta function. The terms involving the different d^K are called differential poles, and the prime number theorem (the Riemann zeta function) plays the role of normalized determinants.
explicit_hypotheses: the notation of Theorem 1.10 and IUTchIII Theorem 3.11
IUT4.Rem1_10_4.conclusion: A terminological analogy: the log-volume fluctuations of Theorem 1.10 are a sort of inter-universal analytic torsion; the different terms are differential poles. No assertion needing proof.
obligations: Nothing to prove; a heuristic remark.

IUT4.Rem1_10_5.content: Computational aspects. (i) Unlike Corollaries 2.2 (ii) and 2.3, the inequalities of Theorem 1.10 have essentially explicit constants and exclude no non-explicit finite set of exceptional elliptic curves, so they suit explicit diophantine computations (for instance Fermat equations), which are not carried out. (ii) Asymptotics: for F_tpd = Q (d_mod = 1) and delta = log(d^{F_tpd}) + log(f^{F_tpd}) = log(f^{F_tpd}), the first bound of the final display of Theorem 1.10 has the form delta + * delta/l + * l + * with fixed positive constants *; the leading term is delta, and the epsilon terms * delta/l + * l are always >= * delta^{1/2} however l is chosen (take l ~ delta^alpha). This is compared with examples of abc sums of Masser and others ([Mss], [vFr] section 2, Equation (6)) whose left side exceeds delta + * delta^{1/2}/log(delta), and with an expectation of van Frankenhuijsen. The paper obtains epsilon terms of order * delta^{1/2} log(delta) under the assumption that the abc sums are compactly bounded away from infinity at 2 and at the archimedean prime (Corollary 2.2 (ii), Remark 2.2.1). (iii) The * l part of the epsilon terms comes from log(s^<=) in Step (viii), which roughly counts prime factors of abc that are <= e*_mod l, related to omega(abc) of [vFr] section 3 and reminiscent of Baker's refinements; examples of [vFr] section 3 Remark 1 with large omega(abc) fit the lower bound of (ii), while sums 2^n = p + q r (p, q, r primes) have omega(abc) <= 4 and left side about half the leading term.
explicit_hypotheses: for (ii): F_tpd = Q, so d_mod = 1; delta = log(f^{F_tpd})
implicit_hypotheses: the constants * in (ii) are fixed positive reals, independent of the initial Theta-data
IUT4.Rem1_10_5.conclusion: (i) The bounds of Theorem 1.10 are effective in form; (ii) with F_tpd = Q the bound has the shape delta + * delta/l + * l + *, whose epsilon terms are >= * delta^{1/2} for every choice of l, consistent with known abc examples; the paper's own bounds on epsilon terms are of order * delta^{1/2} log(delta) under compact boundedness at 2 and infinity; (iii) the * l term comes from log(s^<=) of Step (viii).
obligations: The lower bound >= * delta^{1/2} for the epsilon terms is sketched (compare delta^alpha with delta^{1-alpha}), not proved; the asymptotic claims about the cited examples are taken from [vFr] and [Mss].
ambiguities: Page 34: in (ii) delta is defined as log(d^{F_tpd}) + log(f^{F_tpd}) = log(f^{F_tpd}); with F_tpd = Q this uses that the different of Q is trivial.

IUT4.Rem1_10_6.content: (i) The bound on (1/6) log(q) of Theorem 1.10 concerns only the q-parameters at nonarchimedean places of V_mod^bad, all of odd residue characteristic (IUT I Definition 3.1 (b)); for the [Mss] examples it is not clear how to control the power of 2, but A. Venkatesh pointed out that those examples can be modified to give similar asymptotics without contributions at 2. (ii) Why places of even residue characteristic with bad multiplicative reduction are excluded from V_mod^bad: the theory depends on the etale theta function of [EtTh], which fails at primes over 2, through the simultaneous multiradiality of (1) constant multiple rigidity and (2) cyclotomic rigidity. Evaluating the theta series at the 2-torsion point in the irreducible component labeled zero gives a special value that is a unit for odd p but a nonzero non-unit for p = 2, so the integral structure (a) determined by that value coincides with the integral structure (b) given by the pole at the origin for odd p but not for p = 2; multiradiality of (1) needs (a), and working simultaneously with (b) violates the multiradiality of (2). (iii) It is not clear to the author how far (b) is needed; if (b) plays an essential role as well as (a), the theory is fundamentally incompatible with including even residue characteristic bad places in V_mod^bad. (iv) Classical theta functions and p-adic Teichmueller theory also behave differently or exclude the prime 2.

IUT4.Rem1_10_6.conclusion: Explanatory: the bound of Theorem 1.10 says nothing about q-parameters at places over 2; the exclusion of such places is attributed to the failure at p = 2 of the coincidence of the two integral structures (a), (b) on the theta function, and the author states that it is unclear whether (b) is necessary.

IUT4.Rem1_10_7.content: (i) Since e*_mod <= d*_mod, one may replace e*_mod by d*_mod in the final two displays of the statement of Theorem 1.10. (ii) Within the framework of the series one cannot replace d_mod by e_mod in those displays: the multiradial representation of IUT III Theorem 3.11 (i) uses tensor products over Q of copies of F_mod labeled by j in F_l^* (IUT III Proposition 3.3), whose F_mod-linear structures cannot be identified for distinct labels since the tensor packets may depend only on the additive structure of the mono-analytic log-shells. Localizing at p therefore forces tensor products of localizations of F_mod at distinct primes over p; if one of them lies under a prime of K ramified over Q (condition (D5)), Step (v) produces a log(p) term in log(s^Q) from rounding up non-integral powers of p (Proposition 1.4 (iii)), since only integral powers of p make sense in the multiradial representation.

The j-function of the lambda-line is formalized as a rational function equal to Mathlib's j-invariant of the Legendre curve (IUT4.Cor2_2.frag.legendre_j); the classifying morphism to the moduli stack is not.

IUT4.Cor2_2.frag.legendre_j.content: The j-function of the lambda-line, legendreJ t = 2^8 (t^2 - t + 1)^3 / (t^2 (t - 1)^2), is the Mathlib j-invariant of the Legendre curve whenever that curve is elliptic; legendreJ is invariant under t -> 1 - t and t -> 1/t for every t, and for t != 0 also at (1 - t)^-1, (t - 1)/t and t/(t - 1).
explicit_hypotheses: K a field, t in K
legendreCurve_jInv: the Legendre curve at t is elliptic (instance argument)
IUT4.Cor2_2.frag.legendre_j.conclusion: (legendreCurve t).j = legendreJ t; legendreJ (1 - t) = legendreJ t; legendreJ t^-1 = legendreJ t; the value is the same on the six points of the orbit.
IUT4.Cor2_2.frag.legendre_j.covers: The classifying morphism U_X -> (M_ell)_Q of the lambda-line on page 41, composed with the j-invariant (M_ell)_Q -> A^1 used in condition (*_{j-inv}) on page 41, as an explicit rational function of lambda.
IUT4.Cor2_2.frag.legendre_j.not_covered: The moduli stack, the classifying morphism as a morphism of stacks, condition (*_{j-inv}) on compactly bounded subsets, and every assertion (i) to (iii) of Corollary 2.2. The S3-symmetry is not used on the pages read; it is recorded here as a property of the j-function only.
ambiguities: The formula for j(lambda) is not printed in IUT IV; it is derived from Mathlib's definition of WeierstrassCurve.j.

IUT4.Cor2_2.i.frag.height_j_triple.content: For positive coprime natural numbers a + b = c and lambda = a/c in Q, with h = Height.logHeight1: 6 h(lambda) - log(64/27) <= h(legendreJ lambda) <= 6 h(lambda) + 8 log 2.

IUT4.Cor2_2.ii.content: There are H_unif > 0 independent of K_V, and C_K > 0, H_K > 0 depending only on the choice of K_V, such that: for every positive integer d and real 0 < eps_d <= 1, with delta = 2^12 3^3 5 d, there is a finite set Exc_d in U_X(Qbar)^{<=d}, depending only on K_V, d, eps_d and containing all points of elliptic curves with automorphisms of order > 2, with log(q^forall) <= H_unif eps_d^{-3} d^{4+eps_d} + H_K on Exc_d, such that every elliptic curve E_F over a number field F in Qbar whose moduli point lifts to x_E in U_X(F) intersect U_X(Qbar)^{<=d} with x_E in K_V, x_E not in Exc_d, F_mod its minimal field of definition, F_tpd = F_mod(E_{F_mod}[2]), (3 5)-torsion rational over F and F = F_mod(sqrt(-1), E_{F_mod}[2 3 5]), arises (with F_mod) from initial Theta-data as in Theorem 1.10 satisfying (C1) and (C2); moreover log-diff_X(x_E) = log(d^{F_tpd}) and log(f^{F_tpd}) <= log-cond_D(x_E) <= log(f^{F_tpd}) + log(2l).
explicit_hypotheses: X = P^1 over Q, D = {0, 1, infinity}, regarded as the lambda-line of the Legendre form
K_V a compactly bounded subset of U_X(Qbar) (in the sense of Remark 2.3.1 (vi)) whose support contains the prime 2, satisfying (*_{j-inv})
d a positive integer, eps_d a real number with 0 < eps_d <= 1, delta = 2^12 3^3 5 d
E_F an elliptic curve over a number field F in Qbar with x_E in K_V, x_E not in Exc_d, and F, F_tpd, F_mod as in the statement
implicit_hypotheses: log(q^forall), log(q^{not 2}) the functions of (i); h = log(q^forall) at x_E
IUT4.Cor2_2.ii.conclusion: Existence of H_unif, C_K, H_K and of the finite sets Exc_d with the bound on Exc_d, such that the stated E_F arise from initial Theta-data satisfying (C1) and (C2), together with the equality and inequalities for log-diff_X(x_E) and log-cond_D(x_E).
obligations: Heights on the moduli of elliptic curves, finiteness of j-invariants of bounded height ([GenEll] Proposition 1.4 (iv)), the existence of initial Theta-data and Theorem 1.10 for them are not formalized; the arithmetic of the proof is checked in the fragments of the proof-step records.

The four j-values of the exceptional case and the points of the lambda-line over them are computed (IUT4.Cor2_2.ii.frag.special_j_values); that these are the j-invariants of curves without an F-core is cited, not proved.

IUT4.Cor2_2.ProofP1.content: Proof of (ii), first part (pages 43 to 45). If the once-punctured elliptic curve of E_F has no F-core, there are only four possible j-invariants ([CanLift] Proposition 2.7); putting these into Exc_d, E_F admits an F-core and has no automorphisms of order > 2. Set h = log(q^forall) = (1/[F:Q]) sum_{v in V(F)^non} h_v f_v log(p_v), with h_v = 0 at good reduction and h_v >= 1 the local height ([GenEll] Definition 3.3) at bad multiplicative reduction. Since h^{1/2} < xi_prm leaves finitely many j-invariants (by (i) and [GenEll] Proposition 1.4 (iv)), after enlarging Exc_d (with h <= H_unif on it) one may assume h^{1/2} >= xi_prm >= 5. Using [F:Q] <= delta ((E3), (E4), (E5)): delta h^{1/2} >= [F:Q] h^{1/2} = sum_v h^{-1/2} h_v f_v log(p_v) >= sum_v h^{-1/2} h_v log(p_v) >= sum_{h_v >= h^{1/2}} h^{-1/2} h_v log(p_v) >= sum_{h_v >= h^{1/2}} log(p_v); and 2 delta h^{1/2} log(2 delta h) >= 2 [F:Q] h^{1/2} log(2 [F:Q] h) >= sum_{h_v != 0} 2 h^{-1/2} log(2 h_v f_v log(p_v)) h_v f_v log(p_v) >= sum_{h_v != 0} h^{-1/2} log(h_v) h_v >= sum_{h_v >= h^{1/2}} h^{-1/2} log(h_v) h_v >= sum_{h_v >= h^{1/2}} log(h_v), using 2 log(p_v) >= 2 log 2 = log 4 >= 1. With A the finite set of primes p that (S1) are <= h^{1/2}, (S2) divide a nonzero h_v, or (S3) equal p_v for some v with h_v >= h^{1/2}: theta_A <= 2 h^{1/2} + delta h^{1/2} + 2 delta h^{1/2} log(2 delta h) <= 4 delta h^{1/2} log(2 delta h) <= -xi_prm + 5 delta h^{1/2} log(2 delta h), using delta >= 2 and log(2 delta h) >= log 4 >= 1. Proposition 2.1 (i), (ii) then gives a prime l not in A with (P1), (P2), (P3).
explicit_hypotheses: the situation of Corollary 2.2 (ii); h = log(q^forall) = (1/[F:Q]) sum_v h_v f_v log p_v
IUT4.Cor2_2.ProofP1.conclusion: (P1) (5 <=) h^{1/2} <= l <= 10 delta h^{1/2} log(2 delta h) (<= 20 delta^2 h^2), which is (C1); l is a prime not in A.
obligations: The definition of h through local heights h_v, the bound on theta_A from them (page 44), and the enlargement of Exc_d so that h^{1/2} >= xi_prm (finiteness of j-invariants, [GenEll] Proposition 1.4 (iv)) are not formalized; they are hypotheses of the fragments.

IUT4.Cor2_2.ProofP5.content: (P5): after enlarging Exc_d (with h <= H_unif d + H_K on it), the set V^bad_mod of nonarchimedean valuations of F_mod that do not divide 2l and at which E_F has bad multiplicative reduction is nonempty. IUT4.Rem2_2_1.content: (i) Asymptotics of the bound of Corollary 2.2 (ii) for F_tpd = Q (d_mod = 1), with h = log(q^forall) and delta = log-diff_X(x_E) + log-cond_D(x_E) = log-cond_D(x_E) (a notation different from the delta of Corollary 2.2 (ii)): since 1 < log 3 <= delta and 1 < log 3 <= h, the bound has the form (1/6) h <= delta + * delta^{1/2} log(delta) with a fixed positive *; h/delta is bounded below by definition and above by this bound. The epsilon term delta^{1/2} log(delta) is compared with interpretations of the Riemann hypothesis via weights (a height has the weight of one Tate twist, s = 1, so s = 1/2 corresponds to h^{1/2}, delta^{1/2}); the delta^{1/2} arises as a balance between the archimedean decrease delta/l and the nonarchimedean increase l of the epsilon terms (Steps (v), (viii); the b_i of Proposition 1.4 (iii); the radius of convergence of the p-adic logarithm in Proposition 1.2), likened to the functional equation of zeta. (ii) [vFr] section 2 conjectures limsup log((1/6) h - delta)/log(h) = 1/2; for abc sums in a fixed compactly bounded K_V the bounds of (i) imply limsup <= 1/2, while [vFr] shows limsup >= 1/2 for arbitrary abc sums; whether >= 1/2 holds inside a single K_V is unclear to the author. (iii) Hope for an inter-universal Mellin transform relating the theory to the Riemann zeta function. (iv) Function field analogy: the theory resembles the derivative of a Frobenius lifting, while the function field Riemann hypothesis uses the graph of Frobenius; perhaps an integral of the theory bears on the Riemann hypothesis for number fields. (v) Summary: the Riemann hypothesis inequality might be a restriction (ABC inequality)|_{canonical number} of an ABC inequality to a canonical number, an abstraction of sequences of abc sums, perhaps an average over all addition operations or an arithmetic measure analogous to the one giving the Mellin transform.
explicit_hypotheses: for (i), (ii): the situation of Corollary 2.2 (ii) with F_tpd = Q (d_mod = 1); h = log(q^forall), delta = log-cond_D(x_E)
implicit_hypotheses: * in (i) is a fixed positive real number, independent of x_E
IUT4.Rem2_2_1.conclusion: (i) Under F_tpd = Q, Corollary 2.2 (ii) yields (1/6) h <= delta + * delta^{1/2} log(delta) on K_V outside the exceptional set; (ii) consequently limsup log((1/6) h - delta)/log(h) <= 1/2 for abc sums in a fixed K_V; (iii) to (v) are speculative analogies with the Riemann zeta function and the Riemann hypothesis, not assertions.
obligations: The passage from (C2), with eps_E of order h^{-1/2} log(h), to the form delta + * delta^{1/2} log(delta) in (i) is stated without detail; it needs h and delta comparable, which (i) obtains from the bound itself.

IUT4.Rem2_2_2.content: On weights: the Gaussian integral int_{-infinity}^{infinity} e^{-x^2} dx = sqrt(pi) is viewed as a fundamental integral representation of a Tate semi-twist, while integral values of zeta and L-functions correspond to integral Tate twists, integral powers of 2 pi i (or of pi), the integral of d theta over S^1 equal to 2 pi, and G_m. Scheme-theoretic Hodge-Arakelov theory is a scheme-theoretic representation of a Tate semi-twist. (a) The Gaussian integral, (b) scheme-theoretic Hodge-Arakelov theory, (c) inter-universal Teichmueller theory and (d) the Riemann hypothesis are called phenomena of weight 1/2, the first three reflecting it in an exponential of a quadratic form, reminiscent of (1) Griffiths semi-transversality of the crystalline theta object, (2) the quadratic commutator of the theta group used in [EtTh], and (3) the quadratic nature of the epsilon term * delta/l + * l of Remark 1.10.5 (ii).
IUT4.Rem2_2_2.conclusion: A heuristic grouping of (a) to (d) as phenomena of weight 1/2; the only mathematical fact stated is the Gaussian integral value sqrt(pi) and the integral 2 pi of d theta over S^1.
obligations: Nothing to prove; a heuristic remark.
ambiguities: Page 51: 'fundamental scheme-theoretic represention' is a misprint for 'representation'.

IUT4.Rem2_2_3.content: Remark 2.2.1 concerns Corollary 2.2 (ii) for elliptic curves over Q. If d is an arbitrary (unbounded) positive integer, the inequalities (C2), with Corollary 2.2 (iii), may be regarded as a weak version of the uniform ABC conjecture: weak because they are restricted to points of the compactly bounded subset K_V, and the bounds for log(q^forall) (essentially the height) on Exc_d and Exc_{eps,d} depend on d (cf. IUT4.Rem2_2_4.content: Analogy with p-adic Teichmueller theory ([pOrd], [pTeich], [InpTch]). (i) The log-theta-lattice is compared with the canonical Frobenius lifting on the ordinary locus of a canonical curve over a perfect field; [pOrd] also treats the universal case over the moduli stack of hyperbolic curves with nilpotent ordinary indigenous bundles, smooth of dimension 3g - 3 + r over F_p and far from perfect. The gap between IUT and a canonical number (Remark 2.2.1 (v)) is likened to the gap between canonical curves and the non-perfect moduli stack: canonical number corresponds to modular Frobenius liftings. (ii) Non-perfectness reflects the failure of Frobenius to be an isomorphism; Frobenius corresponds to the log-link, and the * l term of Theorem 1.10 arises from the prime number theorem summing log-volumes of log-shells, which measure distortions of integral structures; l, of the order of the square root of the height by (C1), is a rough numerical representation of the moduli; these observations are said to support the view of (i). (iii) Modular Frobenius liftings live on a p-adic formal stack, not on the algebraic moduli stack; this gap is likened to the gap between compactly bounded subsets K_V (sufficiently general position, a global arithmetic ordinariness) and M_ell(Qbar), bridged in Corollary 2.3 by [GenEll] Theorem 2.1, an arithmetic analytic continuation by Belyi maps, and compared with the open immersion of [InpTch] section 2.6. (iv) The limit l -> infinity is the passage from the discrete approximation by l-torsion points to the full continuous theory, compared with Bernoulli numbers and the passage from f(x) -> f(x+1) - f(x) to d/dx, f(x+1) being e^{d/dx} f.
IUT4.Rem2_2_4.conclusion: A heuristic analogy: canonical number corresponds to modular Frobenius liftings; compactly bounded subsets correspond to ordinary loci; Corollary 2.3 via Belyi maps corresponds to analytic continuation; l -> infinity corresponds to the passage from difference to derivative operators. No assertion needing proof.
obligations: Nothing to prove; a heuristic remark.

For the integral Frey model over Z, an odd prime divides Delta exactly when it divides ab(a + b), and then it does not divide c4.

IUT4.Rem2_3_2.content: (i) Stronger versions of the estimates of Theorem 1.10 and Corollaries 2.2, 2.3 can be obtained with more care, but are not pursued. (ii) The constant 1 in the display of Corollary 2.3 cannot be improved (examples of [Mss]; Remark 1.10.5 (ii), (iii)). This is related to the breakdown of the theory if the first power of the etale theta function is replaced by an N-th power, N >= 2 (Step (xi) of the proof of IUT III Corollary 3.12; IUT III Remark 3.12.1 (ii)), which corresponds to replacing each Tate curve at V^bad by the Tate curve with N-th power q-parameter, an isogeny as in [GenEll] Lemma 3.5; the proof of that lemma shows the global height is essentially unchanged, up to a small discrepancy, under such isogenies, an invariance that is also essential in [Falt].
IUT4.Rem2_3_2.conclusion: (i) Stronger estimates are possible but not given. (ii) The factor 1 multiplying (log-diff_X + log-cond_D) in Corollary 2.3 cannot be replaced by a smaller constant, by the examples of [Mss]; the remark links this to the failure of the theory for N-th powers of the etale theta function and to invariance of heights under isogeny.
obligations: (ii), the optimality of the constant 1, rests on the examples of [Mss], which are not reproduced; (i) is unsubstantiated by design.

IUT4.Rem2_3_3.content: Corollary 2.3 is an effective version of the Mordell conjecture; the remark compares the ingredients of its proof (in effect, of the whole series) with those of [Falt] (discussions with I. Fesenko, summer 2015). (i) A rough list for [Falt]: (a) geometry of numbers, heights, Hermite-Minkowski; (b) global class field theory, dissected following [Lang1] (Weber's approach) into (b-1) local class field theory, (b-2) global density of primes (universal norm index inequality), (b-3) geometry of numbers giving the unit theorem, (b-4) global reciprocity (existence of a conductor for the Artin symbol), (b-5) Kummer theory; (c) p-adic Hodge-Tate decompositions; (d) finite flat group schemes; (e) isogenies and Tate modules; (f) polarizations; (g) logarithmic geometry of toroidal compactifications. (ii) Each is matched with an aspect of IUT: (a), (b-3) with nonzero global integers being roots of unity and with arithmetic degrees and global realified Frobenioids; (b-1) with p-adic absolute anabelian geometry; (b-2) with the prime number theorem (Propositions 1.6, 2.1 (ii)); (b-4) with Q_{>0} intersect Zhat^x = {1} in cyclotomic rigidity; (b-5) with Kummer theory; (c) with [pGC]; (d) with ramification computations for log-shells (Propositions 1.1 to 1.4); (e), (f) with finite etale coverings, Belyi maps, and commutators of theta groups; (g) with combinatorial anabelian geometry. (iii) Summary: aspects of [Falt] are distant abelian, arithmetically holomorphic ancestors of the anabelian, multiradial, mono-analytic theory of IUT; under arithmetic holomorphic structure a Frobenius morphism on a number field (multiplying arithmetic degrees by a factor > 1) cannot exist, while IUT asserts that one can be constructed canonically after dismantling that structure. (iv) The difference is mirrored by global density of primes versus the prime number theorem, which treats primes one by one. (v) Global reciprocity relates local units and local value groups at distinct primes, incompatible with the splittings used in IUT (prime-strips). (vi) Kummer-theoretic isomorphisms are strongly covariantly functorial, while reciprocity maps are not and are ill-suited to evaluating special functions at special points; the price in IUT is the nontrivial cyclotomic rigidity algorithms; local class field theory gives only uniradial algorithms. (vii) Comparison with Kronecker's Jugendtraum and Hilbert's twelfth problem and [Pano]; the author suggests the ideas of IUT resemble late nineteenth and early twentieth century mathematics, and that the course of later mathematics was one possible choice among many.
IUT4.Rem2_3_3.conclusion: An informal comparison of the ingredients of [Falt] with those of IUT, organized as (i) to (vii); its one substantive claim, that Corollary 2.3 is an effective version of the Mordell conjecture, is stated without argument, and the author disclaims completeness or rigor of the list.
external_dependencies: Lang1: Chapters V, VIII, IX, X, XI
obligations: The sense in which Corollary 2.3 is an effective Mordell conjecture (via [GenEll] and Belyi maps) is not explained here; the remainder is a heuristic comparison with nothing to prove.
